content: Cefprozil is prescribed for the treatment of patients with mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible strains of specific microorganisms in the following conditions: 1. Upper Respiratory Tract Infections Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis: Cefprozil is effective against infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. Note: Penicillin administered intramuscularly remains the preferred drug for treating and preventing streptococcal infections, including the prophylaxis of rheumatic fever. While cefprozil is generally effective in eradicating Streptococcus pyogenes from the nasopharynx, there is insufficient evidence to confirm its efficacy in preventing rheumatic fever. Otitis Media: Cefprozil is indicated for infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (including β-lactamase-producing strains), and Moraxella (Branhamella) catarrhalis (including β-lactamase-producing strains). Note: In cases of otitis media caused by β-lactamase-producing organisms, cefprozil has shown slightly lower bacteriologic eradication rates compared to products containing a β-lactamase inhibitor. When considering cefprozil, clinicians should weigh its lower eradication rates against the local susceptibility patterns of common pathogens and the potential for increased toxicity with β-lactamase inhibitor-containing products. Acute Sinusitis: Cefprozil is effective against infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (including β-lactamase-producing strains), and Moraxella (Branhamella) catarrhalis (including β-lactamase-producing strains). 2. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections Secondary Bacterial Infections of Acute Bronchitis and Acute Bacterial Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Cefprozil is indicated for infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (including β-lactamase-producing strains), and Moraxella (Branhamella) catarrhalis (including β-lactamase-producing strains). 3. Skin and Skin Structure Infections Uncomplicated Skin and Skin-Structure Infections: Cefprozil is effective against infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus (including penicillinase-producing strains) and Streptococcus pyogenes. Note: Abscesses typically require surgical drainage in addition to antibiotic therapy. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and preserve the effectiveness of cefprozil and other antibacterial agents, cefprozil should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibiotic therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiology and susceptibility patterns should inform empiric therapy decisions.
